Title: Ni Hsin shifts into high gear with EV diversification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd is diversifying its business into electric vehicles (EVs) as it seeks to scale up its electric motorcycle operations, OEM assembly and market reach.
Ni Hsin, in a Bursa Malaysia filing today, said the proposed diversification will cover EV assembly, promotion and marketing of EVs.
The company wants to build on a business it has operated since 2021 through its subsidiaries Ni Hsin EV Tech Sdn Bhd and EVSend Sdn Bhd.
Ni Hsin currently operates an EV assembly facility in Seri Kembangan, Selangor, where it assembles electric motorcycles using semi-knocked-down and completely knocked-down components.
Its product range includes the Ebixon Torq, Bold and Kruz models, as well as the TC Max and CPX.
The company has also expanded beyond retail sales by targeting corporate, fleet and institutional customers, particularly last-mile logistics operators.
It is further developing its OEM assembly capabilities to attract third-party EV manufacturers.
In April 2026, Ni Hsin EV Tech entered into a contract manufacturing agreement with MARS Greentech Sdn Bhd to assemble selected electric two-wheelers.
The company is also exploring an exclusive local assembly arrangement for Surron electric off-road motorcycles with China-based Chongqing Qiulong Technology Co Ltd.
Overseas expansion is also on the cards. In August, Ni Hsin entered into a memorandum of understanding with Apex Ventures (Labuan) Ltd to promote, market and distribute its products including EVs, initially targeting Turkey and Middle Eastern markets.
However, the EV business remains loss-making.
For the financial year ended June 30 2026, it generated RM1.43 million in revenue but recorded a net loss of RM1.43 million.
In the 18-month financial period ended June 30 2025, EVs contributed 11.07 per cent of group revenue.
Ni Hsin said the proposed diversification aims to position the company to capitalise on the anticipated growth of Malaysia's EV market while creating an additional revenue stream.
The Malaysian EV market expanded sharply in 2025, with new EV registrations rising 104.1 per cent year-on-year to 57,236 vehicles.
The market is forecast to grow another 59.9% in 2026 to 91,527 vehicles and reach 274,401 vehicles by 2030, representing a 36.8 per cent compound annual growth rate.
The company acknowledged risks including intense competition, changing government incentives, rapid technology shifts, reliance on third-party suppliers and partners, and the need to attract skilled EV personnel.
Ni Hsin said the proposed diversification is not expected to have an immediate impact on earnings, net assets or gearing.
It will take effect upon shareholders' approval at an extraordinary general meeting.
M & A Securities Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser for the exercise.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nursery worker to be charged over alleged mistreatment of toddler in Temerloh
Article:
TEMERLOH: The childcare centre worker detained over the alleged rough treatment of a 2-year-old girl at a nursery in Mentakab here last week will be charged tomorrow.
The 25-year-old suspect, who was
remanded yesterday
for six days, will be brought before the magistrate's court here.
Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the woman would be charged under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both upon conviction.
The suspect was arrested on Sept 5, several hours after the victim's mother lodged a police report alleging that her daughter had been subjected to rough treatment by a caregiver at the nursery.
The incident came to light after a
video recording
of the alleged mistreatment went viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak heli crash: A look at the Flying Doctor Service
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For many isolated communities in Malaysia's interior, the Health Ministry's Flying Doctor Service (FDS) is often the difference between receiving healthcare and none at all.
The crash of a FDS helicopter in Long Lellang, Sarawak today has put the service's essential nature into sharp focus.
The
BO-105 helicopter
was carrying five people. Apart from the pilot, those onboard comprised four Health Ministry personnel, namely one medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses.
It is understood that the FDS operated flights to the area on a weekly basis.
The service has operated for decades, with Sarawak's FDS dating back to 1973 and Sabah's to 1978.
It is understood that FDS teams serve numerous remote villages and handle tens of thousands of cases annually while providing regular visits and emergency evacuations.
Health Ministry data also recorded 53 FDS teams and 11 helicopters nationwide as of 2021, underlining that it remains a specialised but important part of the public healthcare infrastructure.
It is essentially a clinic that flies to its patients, providing basic outpatient treatment; maternal and child healthcare; childhood immunisation; screening for infectious diseases such as tuberculosis and malaria; as well as
delivery of medicines and medical supplies.
However, its most critical role is medical evacuation, which is crucial in remote areas, especially in the Sabah and Sarawak interior. The FDS provides a means of transferring patients to the nearest appropriate hospital.
According to the FDS guidelines for Sabah and Sarawak, each mobile aeromedical team consists of a four-person medical crew, comprising one medical officer, one assistant medical officer, and two community nurses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asia is poised to take up 70pct of Canadian oil exports, pipeline executive says
Article:
SINGAPORE: Asia, led by China, is expected to buy 70 per cent of Canadian crude oil exports after the country's only pipeline that provides access to the continent expands its capacity by a third by the end of 2028, a Canadian industry executive said on Tuesday.
* Demand from Asia for Canadian crude has increased as the US-Israeli war on Iran has disrupted supplies from the Middle East.
* The 890,000-barrel-per-day Trans Mountain pipeline from the province of Alberta to British Columbia's west coast, from where oil can be shipped to Asia, hit full capacity for the first time in June.
* Canada's oil output, the world's fourth-largest, this year is set to exceed last year's record of 5.3 million barrels per day, according to Canada's energy regulator.
* Mark Maki, chief executive officer of the pipeline operator Trans Mountain, said the pipeline expansion would add 90,000 barrels per day of transport capacity in the fourth quarter, and another 210,000 barrels per day by the end of 2028.
* "About two-thirds of ships that leave the dock go to Asia and then as we expand, I would expect that most of that (expansion) will be going to Asia," Maki told Reuters on the sidelines of the annual industry gathering APPEC in Singapore.
* Canada in July also announced plans to build an oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific coast, which would give the country greater capacity to export to Asia.
* China, the world's biggest importer of oil, will remain Canada's single largest customer going forward, as heavy Canadian oil is an ideal feedstock for petrochemicals, Maki said.
* Maki said he expected some new countries to become customers, including Thailand, and that India, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam would increase their purchases of Canadian oil.

Title: Moody's sees ongoing surge in Africa's private credit market
Article:
LONDON: Africa's private credit market is set for further expansion as companies and infrastructure projects seek alternatives to constrained bank lending, credit ratings firm Moody's said in a report on Tuesday.
The continent's private credit industry remains small but has grown rapidly in recent years, with assets under management rising to US$5.6 billion at the end of 2025 from US$1.8 billion in 2020, according to the report.
Moody's said demand would continue to be supported by the region's persistent financing gap, underdeveloped capital markets and limits on banks' ability and willingness to provide long-term financing, particularly for infrastructure projects, medium-sized companies and small businesses.
The report added that even after the rapid growth in recent years, Africa accounts for just 0.3 per cent of the global private credit market, which is estimated to be worth at least US$1.8 trillion.
The ratings agency said development finance institutions would remain a key source of funding for the sector in Africa and could help mobilise international capital through credit-enhanced and blended-finance structures.
Such arrangements could support highly rated senior loan tranches and broaden the appeal of African private credit to institutional investors including pension funds and insurers.
At the same time, private credit is unlikely to become a major competitor to African banks, as funds often lend through banks or co-finance transactions, particularly in infrastructure, where financing needs remain substantial.
Moody's said achieving significant scale would require the industry to demonstrate consistent returns that compete with opportunities elsewhere, particularly given investor concerns about frontier-market risk and the mixed historical performance of Africa-focused private investment funds.
The report also highlighted that stock market capitalisation across the continent stood at around 33 per cent of GDP in 2024, well below the respective emerging market and global averages of 61 per cent and 113 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold subdued as oil rises, investors await key US inflation data
Article:
BENGALURU: Gold inched lower on Tuesday as a rise in oil prices reignited inflation fears, while investors remained cautious ahead of crucial data this week that could offer clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate path.
Spot gold fell 0.1 per cent to US$4,400.66 per ounce by 1148 GMT, after rising as much as US$4,442.70 earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.7 per cent to US$4,445.20.
"Gold trades cautiously today, caught between Fed rate hike bets and dollar softness. Higher oil prices stoke inflation risks and expectations for Fed rate hikes, putting the precious metal under pressure," said Nikos Tzabouras, a senior market analyst at Jefferies-owned Tradu.com.
On the geopolitical front, Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthis attacked energy facilities and cities in US ally Saudi Arabia on Tuesday. Oil prices extended gains to multi-week highs.
Spot gold fell as much as 2.4 per cent on Friday after data showed that US job growth accelerated sharply in August, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1 per cent, suggesting an improvement in the labour market.
Traders are now pricing in about a 61 per cent chance of an interest rate hike at the central bank's policy meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool, up from about 50 per cent before the data.
Although gold is typically seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to diminish non-yielding bullion's appeal.
The US dollar index softened, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for buyers overseas.
Investors now await US producer price index data on Thursday and the consumer price index data on Friday for further clues on the Fed's monetary policy stance.
"The precious metal may struggle for firm direction from any inconclusive prints, given fluid market pricing and a Fed that lacks conviction," Tzabouras said.
Among other metals, silver edged 0.2 per cent lower to US$66.03 per ounce, platinum rose 0.1 per cent to US$1,828.50 and palladium slid 1.4 per cent to US$1,368.80.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly man killed after being hit by SUV in Assam Jawa
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: An elderly man was killed after he was thrown from his motorcycle when it was hit by a sports utility vehicle (SUV) at KM42.7 of the Klang-Teluk Intan Road near Assam Jawa here today.
Kuala Selangor deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Ambia Nordin said the 3.50pm accident resulted in the 67-year-old victim dying at the scene.
He said the crash involved a Perodua Kembara SUV and a Yamaha Ego LC motorcycle.

Title: Public Bank offers RM1.29 a share to take Hong Kong listed unit private
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd is proposing to privatise its 73.23 per cent-owned Hong Kong-listed subsidiary Public Financial Holdings Ltd at HK$2.50 (RM1.29) a share via a scheme of arrangement.
The cash offer will cost Public Bank about HK$734.75 million to buy the remaining 26.77 per cent stake, or 293.9 million shares, according to the banking group's bourse filing on Tuesday.
Public Bank said the offer price will not be increased.
The proposed offer represents a 61.29 per cent premium to Public Financials' closing price of HK$1.55 on Aug 19, the last trading day before the announcement.
It is also an 83.82 per cent premium to Public Financial's average daily closing price of HK$1.44 over the 360 trading days up to Aug 19.
However, the offer comes at a steep 64.64 per cent discount to PFHL's unaudited consolidated net asset value of HK$7.08 a share as at June 30.
Public Financial's businesses span banking and financial services, stockbroking, investment property leasing, financing for taxi and public light-bus purchasers and taxi trading and leasing.
Its banking operations comprise 29 branches in Hong Kong and one in China, according to Public Financial's website.
Public Bank said the proposals give scheme shareholders with an opportunity to realise their investment immediately at an attractive premium to the historical trading prices of Public Financial's shares.
The bank noted that trading liquidity in Public Financial shares has been relatively low.
In the 12 months up to and including the last trading day, the average daily trading volume accounted for just 0.027 per cent of Public Financial's total issued shares, with average daily turnover of about HK$414,000.
"In these circumstances, a scheme shareholder wishing to dispose of a sizeable shareholding through the market may not be able to do so within a short period without potentially affecting the prevailing market price," it added.
Public Bank said the proposed privatisation would also simplify Public Financial's ownership structure, while allowing closer alignment and more efficient coordination between it and the banking group.
Taking Public Financial private would further eliminate the costs and administrative requirements associated with maintaining its stock market listing, enabling resources to be directed more closely towards its banking operations, the bank said.
For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Public Financial recorded operating income of HK$692.22 million and net profit of HK$25.19 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Husband told of Dr Ainul's death in Sarawak heli crash
Article:
KOTA BARU: "Our family was contacted by the Health Ministry (MOH) this afternoon and informed that Dr Ainul had died."
Nureez Mohd Pauzi, Dr Ainul's sister-in-law, said Dr Ainul had been identified as one of the passengers on the helicopter reported to have crashed and caught fire near Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram here this afternoon.
She said the call from the MOH was made to Dr Ainul's husband, Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, at around 4pm.
"Our family is now at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport to travel to Kuala Lumpur before departing for Sarawak at dawn tomorrow.
"We are shocked. The earliest flight to Sarawak is tomorrow morning. As soon as we received the call, the family immediately bought flight tickets to Sarawak," she said.
She said Dr Ainul, who was from Kota Bharu, had been working at a hospital in Miri since last year.
"She previously served at Tanah Merah Hospital before transferring to Miri to follow her husband, who works as a teacher there.
"As of now, we do not know where Dr Ainul was heading when she boarded the helicopter, as her husband is also still in shock and only informed us about the call from the Health Ministry," she said.
Earlier, a Bo-105 helicopter carrying five people, including its pilot, was reported to have crashed near Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), in a statement, confirmed the incident.
CAAM said it received notification of the crash from the Flight Information Services at 3.58pm.
Besides Dr Ainul Baroah, the other four people on board were the pilot and three Health Ministry personnel, including two nurses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Dr Ainul' confirmed as among deceased in Sarawak heli crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The identity of one of the passengers of the B0-105 helicopter which crashed near the Long Lellang airstrip today has been identified.
Medical Officer Dr Ainul Baroah Kamaruddin, from Kelantan, was among those onboard the aircraft.
It is learnt that her family was told that she had died in the crash.
She was among five people, including the pilot, on the flight.
The fate of the rest remain unknown for now.
A picture of Dr Ainul, seated in a helicopter with others believed to be Health Ministry personnel, was widely circulated today following the crash.
It has since been established that the picture (posted on March 10) was from a Facebook account belonging to Alexson Adit, an assistant medical officer with the ministry.
In the same picture, Alexson, in green, is seated in front next to the pilot,
He is also believed to be among those on board but his status remains unknown at the moment.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the SAR team was rushing to the site from the Marudi district police headquarters, a journey which normally takes 10 hours by road.
He said police would also use air services to reach the location, subject to approval by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
If allowed to do so, the team would depart from the Kuching Airbase.
Approval for the journey is needed due to hazy conditions.
CAAM, in a statement earlier, confirmed the incident involving a helicopter bearing the registration number 9M-LLF. The helicopter was carrying five people, including the pilot and was operating the Flying Doctors Service flight.
The
B)-105 helicopter
is a light, twin-engine helicopter manufactured in Germany and known for its use in a wide range of civilian and military roles.
It is widely associated with air rescue operations worldwide.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Locally assembled EX90: Volvo's electric flagship arrives
Article:
VOLVO Car Malaysia has launched the evolved EX90, Volvo's fully electric seven-seat flagship SUV, with the locally assembled model positioned as a new benchmark for premium electric mobility.
Priced from RM428,888 excluding insurance, the EX90 is available for viewing at authorised dealers nationwide.
Early adopters will receive a RM25,000 cash rebate and RM3,990 Volvo Wallbox, with the offer limited to the first 100 units booked.
Volvo's flagship continues the brand's safety-first philosophy through its Safe Space Technology, combining radars, sensors and ultrasonic sensors to create a detailed real-time view around the vehicle.
Inside, an advanced Driver Understanding System uses two infrared sensors to monitor signs of driver distraction or impairment, while an Occupant Sensing System can detect even subtle movements to help ensure passengers - including children - are not inadvertently left behind.
The EX90 also features the latest Pilot Assist and Park Pilot Assist, adding enhanced driver support and collision-avoidance capabilities.
Underpinning the EX90 is an upgraded 800-volt electrical architecture paired with a Twin Motor all-wheel-drive system.
The setup produces 680hp and 870Nm, enabling a 0-100km/h sprint in just 4.2 seconds.
A 106kWh battery provides up to 617km of WLTP range, while 350kW DC fast charging can take the battery from 10 per cent to 80 per cent in about 22 minutes.
The EX90 is also Volvo's software-defined flagship, now powered by an Nvidia DRIVE AGX Orin-based core computer to manage safety systems, sensors, battery functions and other vehicle operations.
Its Superset technology stack enables regular over-the-air updates, allowing features and performance to evolve throughout the vehicle's lifetime.
Inside, Google-built infotainment services, a 14.5-inch centre display and Bowers & Wilkins high-fidelity audio combine with Scandinavian-inspired materials and a choice of Nappa leather interiors.
The EX90's clean, flush exterior reflects Volvo's minimalist Scandinavian design philosophy, while an electrochromic roof allows occupants to adjust light and cabin temperature.
Five exterior colours are available, including Onyx Black, Sand Dune, Crystal White, Vapour Grey and Mulberry Red.
Volvo is also updating its electric saloon, the ES90, for model year 2027 with new exterior colours, a Cardamom interior option, new 21-inch wheels and wireless Android Auto.
Early bookings are eligible for cash rebates of up to RM17,600, with orders opening from this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump sparks fury with post of map with Canada, Iceland as part of US
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has sparked fury by posting a map that seemingly showed Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico and the Caribbean as part of the United States.
Monday's post – the latest of several from Trump with an outlandish territorial design – came amid a flurry of around 100 messages on his Truth Social platform over the Labour Day weekend.
Iceland responded to the new map post on Tuesday, announcing that it had summoned the US ambassador to make it clear that the image was "wholly inappropriate."
The map showed the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico and the Caribbean coloured in with the US flag.
The entire landmass was labelled "United States of America" and the image was posted without any further explanation.
Trump unleashed his avalanche of posts at breakneck pace – around 60 on Sunday alone and 37 in 10 hours on Monday, according to an AFP count, relying as he often does on artificial intelligence.
Trump also posted a cartoon of himself playing in an ice hockey match against Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
In the image, Trump tells Carney, who is lying on the ice: "Get up governor."
Canada is locked in a trade war in Washington, with retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products taking effect Tuesday.
Trump has also made insistent claims that Canada should become the 51st US state.
In another post, an image showed Trump receiving George Washington in the Oval Office.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: College student killed in Marang lorry crash
Article:
MARANG: A college student was killed after his motorcycle was hit by a lorry on Jalan Bukit Kor near Kampung Rhu Rendang here today.
The victim, Muhammad Afiq Izzuddin Azhar, 18, was pronounced dead at the scene following the accident at 1.10pm.
Marang district police chief Superintendent Saari Mohamed said the accident involved an Isuzu lorry driven by a 34-year-old man and a Honda C100 motorcycle ridden by the victim.
He said initial investigations found that both vehicles were travelling in the same direction when the victim, who was riding along the left shoulder of the road, suddenly made a U-turn.
The lorry, which was travelling behind the motorcycle, then struck the victim's motorcycle, he said.
"The victim, who was from Kuala Berang, was seriously injured and pronounced dead at the scene.
"The lorry driver, however, was uninjured and a urine test conducted on him was negative," he said.
Saari said the victim's body was sent to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital in Kuala Terengganu.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flying doctor helicopter was carrying four Health Ministry personnel, pilot - Dzulkefly
Article:
MIRI: The Health Ministry Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter that crashed here today was carrying four ministry personnel and a pilot.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said those on board were a medical officer, assistant medical officer and two nurses, who were on official duty.
It reportedly
crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) port
in Sarawak this evening.
Dzulkefly said the status of the pilot and four passengers, as well as the cause of the incident, had yet to be confirmed.
The
helicopter, a BO-105, is a light,
twin-engine aircraft originally developed in Germany and known for its use in a wide range of civilian and military roles.
"Search and rescue (SAR) teams, together with medical personnel and the Fire and Rescue Department, are at the scene and the operation is ongoing," he said in a statement today.
Dzulkefly said the ministry was closely monitoring the situation and working with security authorities, rescue teams and relevant aviation agencies to obtain accurate and updated information from the scene.
He said the ministry was also in the process of contacting the next-of-kin and family members of those involved to provide the necessary support.
"As the SAR operation is still ongoing, I urge the media and public not to speculate or spread unverified information out of respect for the feelings of the victims' families," he said.
He added that further developments would be announced once they had been officially confirmed by the authorities.
"Let us pray that the search and rescue operation will be facilitated," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu under fire over report UAE warned of Oct 7 attack
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the United Arab Emirates had warned him before the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack.
Haaretz newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation.
Netanyahu's office called the report by the left-leaning newspaper "an absolute lie" and denied he spoke to the Emirati leader at that time.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander who has emerged as Netanyahu's top rival in upcoming Oct 27 elections, accused the long-serving prime minister of evading responsibility for security lapses and resorting to "pathetic" excuses, such as saying he was not woken up soon enough on the morning of the attack.
"Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for Oct 7 and ignored them all. He is unfit," Eisenkot wrote on X.
Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in elections, said Netanyahu "bears personal and direct responsibility" for the deaths on Oct 7, the deadliest attack in Israeli history.
"Netanyahu cannot continue to serve in his position for even one more minute," Bennett said.
The leader of the centre-left Democrats Party, Yair Golan, accused Netanyahu of "endangering Israel."
"The stories about 'no one woke me up' are over. You knew, you ignored, you failed, you are to blame," he said in a video posted on social media.
'Earthquake'
Many Israelis have demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into the security lapses that failed to prevent Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack.
Opposition parties say establishing such a commission – whose members would be appointed by the Supreme Court – would be their first priority if elected.
But Netanyahu's government has rejected the proposal.
Haaretz said that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar, later killed by Israel, had warned a former Palestinian official that the fighters were preparing "a terrifying operation" which he described as an "earthquake."
The former Palestinian official relayed the message to an Emirati adviser, who passed it on to the Emirati leader who then called Netanyahu, according to the newspaper.
The UAE normalised ties with Israel in 2020 as part of the US-brokered Abraham Accords under President Donald Trump's first administration.
Netanyahu sees close ties with the UAE as a key achievement.
The newspaper, quoting mostly anonymous sources, said that Netanyahu replied calmly to the warning.
Netanyahu for years had sought to preserve the status quo with Hamas, which would receive funding via Qatar with an understanding the fighter group was more interested in self-preservation than a devastating war with Israel.
Hamas on Oct 7 stormed into Israel in a rampage that included mass killing at a music festival.
The attack killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. The fighters also dragged into Gaza some 251 hostages, 44 of them already dead.
The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed 73,658 people, according to the Gaza health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Budget 2027 should prioritise high-quality jobs to boost disposable income
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to focus on creating high-quality, high-impact job opportunities through Budget 2027 to increase the people's disposable income.
Prof Dr Mohd Abdullah Jusoh, of the Department of Logistics Management and Business Administration, Faculty of Defence Studies and Management, Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia  (UPNM), said economic stimulus measures should shift towards empowering the workforce with skills that would enable them to become self-reliant and earn higher incomes.
He said financial assistance schemes such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) are effective in easing the people's financial burden and providing an immediate economic boost, but a long-term strategy requires the development of new economic engines.
"Rather than merely providing aid, it is better to create new job opportunities for them so they can stand on their own feet," he said when appearing as a guest on the Malaysia Petang Ini programme produced by Bernama TV here today.
Commenting on the national economic outlook, Mohd Abdullah said Malaysia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 reflected an encouraging performance compared with World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates of between 2.5 and three per cent.
However, he stressed that aggregate economic growth must be balanced with efforts to ensure that the resulting prosperity directly benefits households through higher wages and stronger purchasing power.
On the national inflation rate of 1.8 per cent, he described government interventions as effective in preventing the prices of staple food items from rising sharply.
"Price increases for staple foods remain under control, perhaps at around one or 1.5 per cent. While this may not have a drastic impact on consumers generally, any increase still affects the B40 and vulnerable groups," he said.
Mohd Abdullah also hoped that Budget 2027 would place greater emphasis on the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ecosystem and the gig economy, enabling both to evolve into more sustainable professional career pathways for young people.
He said empowering both the private and public sectors to create job opportunities based on three key elements — growth, sustainability and value addition — is crucial to ensuring the nation's long-term economic prosperity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Green factors increasingly shape Malaysians' property decisions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sustainability and climate resilience are increasingly influencing Malaysians' property decisions, alongside price, size and location, according to PropertyGuru Malaysia's first half of 2026 consumer sentiment study.
The study found that 86 per cent of Malaysians consider sustainable features important when buying or renting a home.
Seventy-eight per cent take climate risks into account when purchasing property, with flooding and landslides among the key concerns.
It also found that 93 per cent of Malaysians are willing or open to paying more for properties with green features.
This reflects a growing interest in factors such as energy efficiency, ventilation, water use, solar readiness and electric vehicle (EV) charging access.
Climate resilience is also becoming a consideration for home seekers, who are increasingly looking at how properties and their locations may be affected by risks such as flooding, landslides and heat, as well as drainage conditions.
Neighbourhood quality remains important, with 36 per cent of Malaysians prioritising security and safety when selecting a property, while 30 per cent prioritise infrastructure and amenities.
The study found that 52 per cent of Malaysians have lived in their current residence for more than 10 years, highlighting the importance of choosing homes and neighbourhoods that can support their daily needs over the long term.
Family and life-stage needs are also influencing property decisions, with 64 per cent of Malaysians living with a spouse, 38 per cent with parents, 38 per cent with young children and 21 per cent with adult children.
Among those intending to buy a property, 19 per cent said they were doing so because they needed more space for children or parents, indicating that home-buying decisions are also closely linked to family and long-term living needs.
PropertyGuru head of sustainability Cécile Corda said a future-ready home is not just about its location, size and price alone.
It is also about how well it can adapt to people's evolving life stages and needs, while being prepared for a changing climate and the risks that come with it.
"Through Gurus For Good, particularly our Sustainable Living focus, PropertyGuru aims to make sustainability more practical and relevant to the property journey.
"Our role is to help Malaysians build a more complete picture of what matters throughout their property journey, so they can make more informed decisions," she said in a statement.
The report outlines PropertyGuru's sustainability strategy, which focuses on sustainable living, thriving communities and responsible business.
The sustainable living pillar reflects PropertyGuru's commitment to making sustainability more visible and useful in the property journey, helping property seekers consider sustainable features alongside traditional factors such as price, location and space.
PropertyGuru said as Malaysians think more holistically about home, choosing a property increasingly means looking beyond the immediate transaction to consider comfort, cost, climate resilience, family, access, safety and community.
It added that these considerations are becoming increasingly important as Malaysians look for homes that meet their long-term needs and changing lifestyles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Huawei heads to trial in US over its business dealings in Iran
Article:
NEW YORK: Eight years after US prosecutors secretly charged China's Huawei Technologies with defrauding HSBC and other banks over its business with Iran, the case is finally heading for trial.
Huawei also faces charges for conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US technology companies, and is accused of lying about its dealings in North Korea and supplying surveillance equipment to Iran to track protesters during 2009 anti-government demonstrations in Tehran.
Jury selection is expected to begin on Tuesday in federal court in Brooklyn, New York.
The trial will bring to a close one of the US government's earliest and most closely watched battles against a Chinese company, and will play out as tech competition heats up between the two countries and Washington seeks to prevent American technology from aiding Beijing.
The US-China tech war has now spread across multiple technology sectors, including artificial intelligence.
The saga began in 2018 with the arrest of Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou in Vancouver, which sparked a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.
Convictions on the Iran-related charges would bolster Washington's case for having placed Huawei, one of China's leading technology companies, on a US trade blacklist in 2019, citing alleged criminal conduct that threatened national security.
The trial before US District Judge Ann Donnelly is expected to last about three months and overlap with Chinese President Xi Jinping's September 24 meeting with President Donald Trump in Washington. Potential jurors have filled out 27-page questionnaires, including about their views on China's and Iran's governments.
Other charges include violating US sanctions against Iran, money laundering, racketeering, wire fraud and obstruction. Huawei has pleaded not guilty on all charges and denied any wrongdoing.
The criminal case is based in part on reporting by Reuters in 2012 and 2013 about close ties between Huawei and Skycom, a firm that operated in Iran.
Reuters reported that Skycom had offered to sell at least €1.3 million (US$1.5 million) worth of embargoed Hewlett-Packard computer equipment to Iran's largest mobile-phone operator in 2010. Reuters also reported that Meng had served on Skycom's board of directors between February 2008 and April 2009. The coverage can be read here and here.
## BEIJING SAYS CASE AIMS TO UNDERMINE CHINESE TECH
Beijing has long criticised the case, saying it was part of a bigger campaign against China's technological rise. A Huawei spokesperson said in a statement on Saturday, "The government's overarching narrative is demonstrably false."
Today Huawei is a centrepiece of China's AI chip ambitions, and has diversified beyond network gear and smartphones. It has described the criminal case as an effort to undermine its competitiveness and the theft accusations as a repackaging of long-resolved commercial disputes.
If Huawei is convicted, prosecutors will seek the forfeiture of property or proceeds obtained from its illegal activity.
The case against the company was brought during the first Trump administration, which also took actions to curb the use of Huawei equipment in the US and pressed other countries to drop Huawei from their telecommunications networks, saying China could use its equipment for espionage.
The indictment covers alleged wrongdoing between about 1999 and 2020.
It accuses Huawei of using Skycom to obtain embargoed US goods, technology and services for Huawei's Iran-based business, and to move money out of that country through the international banking system.
The US said one bank, which was not named in the indictment but which sources and documents reviewed by Reuters identified as HSBC, cleared more than US$100 million worth of US-dollar transactions related to Skycom.
Prosecutors accused Meng of misrepresenting Huawei's ownership and control of Skycom in a presentation to an HSBC executive. She later admitted the statements were false, as part of an agreement with prosecutors to drop the charges against her.

Title: Penang police chief: No compromise on misconduct
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said integrity, discipline and honesty were essential to policing duties.
Speaking at the September monthly assembly at the Penang police contingent headquarters here today, Lim said there would be no compromise on abuse of power, extortion or attempts to shield criminals.
"Firm action will be taken against any personnel found guilty of misconduct, regardless of rank, position or status," he said.
Lim also directed investigating officers to understand and comply with legal provisions, particularly those involving remand applications, while ensuring all actions were based on clear, reasonable and transparent grounds.
He said investigating officers, heads of divisions and supervisory officers must closely monitor investigations to ensure cases were handled professionally and free from external influence.
In line with Inspector-General of Police Directive No. 191 on "Total Enforcement" of Regulation 3C, he said indications of misconduct, negligence or disciplinary weaknesses must be identified and addressed immediately.
Lim also called for comprehensive preparations for the "Whitening the Blackspot: United For Safety" crime prevention initiative, which requires close cooperation between police, the government, relevant agencies, the private sector and communities.
At the event, Lim presented certificates of appreciation to 20 recipients in recognition of their excellence, commitment and contributions to the force.
He also urged personnel to strengthen teamwork, set aside personal interests and discharge their duties with dedication, professionalism and integrity to safeguard public safety, order and community wellbeing.
Also present were Penang deputy police chief Datuk Abdul Rahman Kassim, state Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zailanni Amit, Special Branch chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zakaria A. Rahim, Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Helmi Aris, department and formation heads, district police chiefs, senior and junior police officers and civilian personnel.

Title: East Coast poised to become food security hub, green economy leader – MIDA
Article:
KUANTAN: Malaysia's East Coast region has strong potential to become a key hub for national food security and a leading centre for the green economy through greater investment in renewable energy.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chief executive officer, Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid, said smart farming, food processing, cold-chain infrastructure, and logistics could boost productivity and strengthen the country's food supply chain.
He said the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) would further improve connectivity and market access for agrofood products by facilitating the movement of raw materials and finished products to wider markets.
"Connectivity through the ECRL will also expand market access for agrofood products, while facilitating the movement of raw materials and products to wider markets," he said in his speech at the 2026 East Coast Region Investment Seminar here today.
Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim indicated that Pahang, Terengganu, and Kelantan have significant potential in renewable energy, especially in solar, biomass, and hydropower, including floating solar-hydro hybrid projects.
He said such development was in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and the Green Investment Strategy, creating opportunities for high-technology, sustainable and environmentally friendly investments.
The East Coast region recorded RM61.4 billion in approved investments between 2021 and June 2026, involving 1,746 projects expected to create more than 30,000 jobs, said Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim.
He urged Bumiputera companies, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and mid-tier companies in the region to explore the capital market as an alternative source of financing, including through initial public offerings (IPOs).
"This is important to enable local companies to move to the next level and become industry role models amid increasingly challenging global supply-chain competition," he said.
Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim said the implementation of the New Incentive Framework (NIF) would place greater emphasis on high-impact, high-technology and sustainable investments in line with the needs of the future economy.
MIDA, through its Incentives Coordination and Collaboration Office (ICCO) and i-Incentives Portal, also facilitates access by local companies, particularly SMEs and Bumiputera firms, to relevant government support and incentives.
Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim emphasised that companies should make full use of the 84 active incentive schemes offered by 10 ministries through the i-Incentives Portal to strengthen their business capabilities.
He added that MIDA, together with federal and state agencies, was ready to expedite approvals and address project implementation issues through the Invest Malaysia Facilitation Centre (IMFC).
Meanwhile, Pahang state Business and Investment Officer Datuk Kamarul 'Arifin Ahmad @ Abd Rahman, representing the state government, expressed appreciation to MIDA for organising the seminar in Kuantan.
He said the event would help unlock new investment opportunities and stimulate economic growth in the East Coast region.
More than 400 participants attended the seminar, which also featured an appreciation and pre-listing showcase recognising Pahang-based aquaculture firm FDI Group and Terengganu-based oil and gas engineering company Upstream Downstream Process & Services Sdn Bhd.

Title: 81-year-old woman dies after being run over in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: An 81-year-old woman died after she was run over by a vehicle at the Desa Green flats parking area in Solok Slim here today.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received information about the fatal accident at 3.50pm.
"Initial investigations found that the victim had alighted from a GrabCar about 2.20pm and was walking towards her block when she tripped and fell onto the road.
"A vehicle, believed to be a car, then drove straight ahead and struck the victim before fleeing the scene without stopping," he said.
Abdul Rozak said the woman was pronounced dead at the scene at 2.48pm after sustaining head injuries.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Those with information about the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Irwandy Hamled at 013-5155656," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Explainer: How remote is Long Lellang, where helicopter crashed?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Long Lellang, a remote settlement comprising two villages, Long Lellang A and Long Lellang B, came into the spotlight today after a
helicopter crashed
there.
There were five people on board the helicopter, including the pilot, but there has been no word as to their fates.
Police have since
mobilised a search and rescue
team.
Long Lellang residents are mostly from the Kelabit and Penan communities.
WHERE IS LONG LELLANG?
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia's website, Long Lellang is located near the Sarawak-Kalimantan border, in the same region as Bario and Long Banga.
It can take between four and six days to hike there through thick jungle.
The village is under the Marudi district in Miri.
HOW FAR IS IT FROM THE NEAREST TOWNS?
Marudi is about six hours away by road, while Miri is about seven hours away by road.
HOW DO SUPPLIES REACH LONG LELLANG?
General rations and food supplies are brought in from Miri, while local produce, including coffee and rice, is marketed outside the settlement.
Cargo and fuel can also be transported by longboat.
The journey takes about two hours, after which the cargo is transferred to a car for the remainder of the journey to Marudi.
WHAT FACILITIES ARE AVAILABLE?
Despite its remote location, Long Lellang has a primary school and a clinic, as well as weekly flying doctor services.
WHO USES THE AIR SERVICE?
Passengers include retirees, teachers, nurses and government officials.
HOW MANY PASSENGERS TRAVEL TO AND FROM LONG LELLANG?
An average of 1,960 passengers travelled to and from Long Lellang annually between 2016 and 2019.
The number of passengers was 1,847 in 2016, 2,199 in 2017, 2,247 in 2018 and 1,548 in 2019.
The figures are from MasWings.

Title: DAP wants equal constituency funding, starting with Penang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP wants the Penang government to enact a Constituency Development Fund (CDF) law to ensure development allocations are distributed fairly and equally to all assemblymen, regardless of political affiliation.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke, in a statement yesterday, said the party's Central Executive Committee (CEC) had resolved to ask the Penang government to enact a CDF Enactment, reflecting a reform agenda long championed by Pakatan Harapan (PH).
If implemented, Penang would become the first state to introduce such a law.
Loke said he believes the same principle of fairness should similarly be extended to the federal level and adopted by other state governments.
Loke said the decision was among several reform matters discussed at the CEC's first meeting following the DAP National Conference on Aug 16.
The party also wants two major constitutional reform agendas — the separation of powers between the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, and a 10-year term limit for the prime minister — to be debated and decided during Parliament's upcoming October sitting.
The Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill 2026 to separate the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor aims to provide for the appointment of a Public Prosecutor in line with the separation of the Public Prosecutor's role from the Attorney General.
It also aims to provide safeguarding provisions for the Public Prosecutor and amend related matters in accordance with that separation of roles.
Meanwhile, the Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure aims, among other things, to restrict the office of the Prime Minister to a maximum of 10 years.
Loke said the CEC meeting also discussed the outcome of the National Conference regarding the motion passed by delegates to mandate the party leadership of DAP to remain in the federal government until the end of the 15th Parliament term.
"The CEC respects the decision made by the delegates and is determined to carry out that mandate with full responsibility. DAP will continue striving to ensure that various reform agendas can be implemented," he said.
Loke added that the CEC meeting also discussed preparations for the Melaka and Sarawak state elections, including efforts to defend all seats currently held by DAP and to identify potential seats to contest.

Title: Lim Guan Eng criticises Pas over lottery draw claims
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: DAP advisor Lim Guan Eng has criticised Pas over its claims concerning the party's stance on lottery draws.
Lim said he was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 to eight times a year during the Pakatan Harapan administration from 2018 to 2020.
"Pas is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year when the PH government ruled from 2018 to 2020," he said in his Facebook posting.
Lim claimed the number of draws was subsequently increased to 22 times a year by the Pas, Umno, Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional coalition government in 2020 and remained at that level until the end of the BN-PN administration in 2022.
Lim said Pas did not need to praise him but questioned why the party continued to accuse DAP leaders of being opposed to Islam.
"I don't need Pas to praise me. But the question is why does Pas like to slander DAP leaders as opposing Islam when DAP only opposes Pas and its politics of hatred and lies?" he asked.
He said it was now up to the people to decide whether Pas' political approach was inconsistent with its principles and amounted to hypocrisy.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently defended the government's decision to cut special lottery draws from 22 to eight annually, saying he does not support gambling.
Anwar said the reduction was made after he became prime minister, countering criticism that he supported gambling.
Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor had criticised Anwar over the issue of gambling premises licences in the state.

Title: Ringgit ends lower as oil prices rise, Fed decision looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed lower against the US dollar on Tuesday, weighed by higher crude oil prices and cautious sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) next policy decision, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the local currency eased to 4.0605/0640 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0440/0485.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said elevated crude oil prices could strengthen the case for a Fed rate hike next week.
"Other Asian currencies were also mixed, with the (US) dollar-yen hovering at 153 yen as expectations of a Bank of Japan rate hike next week gathered further momentum.
"In a nutshell, market sentiment was anxious about the Fed's next move in the near term," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit was lower against a basket of major currencies.
It slipped against the euro to 4.7151/7191 from Monday's 4.6991/7044, weakened against the British pound to 5.4926/4974 from 5.4736/4796, and declined against the Japanese yen to 2.6374/6398 from 2.6173/6204.
The ringgit also traded lower against most regional currencies.
It inched down against the Philippine peso to 6.48/6.49 from 6.46/6.47 on Monday and declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.2073/2104 from 3.1943/1981.
It fell against the Thai baht to 12.3285/3447 from 12.3041/3231 and weakened against the Indonesian rupiah to 230.3/230.5 from 229.2/229.6 at the previous close.

Title: Porsche heritage meets the future at Luftwasser 2026
Article:
PORSCHE Malaysia, represented by Sime Darby Auto Performance, joined hundreds of owners and enthusiasts at Luftwasser 2026: Icona Heritage, celebrating the marque's heritage, motorsport and future-facing technology.
Held at LYL International Karting Circuit, the independently organised gathering featured Porsche models spanning generations - from air-cooled and water-cooled classics to GTs, special editions, racing cars and the latest road-going models.
"Every Porsche has an engine, but it is the community that gives the brand its heartbeat," said Christopher Hunter, chief executive officer of Sime Darby Auto Performance.
He described Luftwasser as a gathering that connects owners and enthusiasts through their shared passion for Porsche.
Motorsport was a major theme, with the event marking 75 years of Porsche Motorsport - a legacy that began with the Porsche 356 SL's class victory at Le Mans in 1951.
Porsche Malaysia highlighted this heritage through a display of racing cars from different eras, alongside current road models, illustrating how lessons from competition continue to influence Porsche's sports cars.
The display also traced Porsche Malaysia's customer racing journey, featuring 911 GT3 Cup cars from the 997, 991 and current 992.2 generations.
The latest car is campaigned by Naquib Azlan and Team Porsche Malaysia in the 2026 Porsche Carrera Cup Asia season.
The new Cayenne Electric made its appearance alongside its predecessors, showcasing more than two decades of evolution for Porsche's performance SUV.
With up to 1,156 PS, a WLTP range of up to 669km and DC charging of up to 400kW, the Cayenne Electric is billed as Porsche's most powerful production model yet.
Its 800-volt architecture enables a 10-80 per cent charge in less than 16 minutes under optimal conditions.
The model is available to order in Malaysia from RM699,000, complementing existing combustion and plug-in hybrid Cayenne variants.
Visitors also received a public preview of the Porsche 911 Challenge, an accessible entry point into customer motorsport.
Powered by a naturally aspirated 4.0-litre flat-six producing 515 PS, the race car pairs its engine with a seven-speed PDK transmission derived from the road-going 911 GT3.
Beyond the cars, Luftwasser 2026 highlighted the people behind Porsche culture.
Test drives, racing simulators, a Porsche Lifestyle boutique and the hospitality paddock gave owners and newcomers opportunities to connect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil hits multi-week highs after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities
Article:
BENGALURU: Oil prices hit multi-week highs on Tuesday after Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi energy facilities and Tehran threatened the United States with "economic warfare".
Brent crude futures were up US$1.39, or 1.43 per cent, at US$98.39 a barrel at 0956 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$93.73 a barrel, up US$2.25, or 2.46 per cent.
Brent earlier rose to US$99.46, its highest since July 24, while WTI reached US$94.73, its highest since June 8.
"The price action reflects both genuine physical tightness — tanker flows through Hormuz remain well below normal — and a clear geopolitical risk premium. Right now the risk premium is doing a lot of the heavy lifting," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
"As for the rest of the year, oil looks set to remain elevated while the Strait stays contested and diplomatic progress remains fragile."
Operations at some energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, were halted on Tuesday following attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that wounded 73 people, in what Saudi authorities called a dangerous escalation.
Meanwhile, Iran threatened the United States with "economic warfare" and said it had fired an advanced missile at US warships, underscoring the risks of further escalation in the war only days after both sides traded blows again.
On Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The attacks followed strikes by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region.
Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz also slowed at the start of this week, after Iran threatened on Monday to retaliate for any new US attacks.
The Strait of Hormuz handled about one-fifth of global daily oil and liquefied natural gas supplies before the conflict began in late February.
Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised its Brent and WTI price forecasts by US$5 to US$85 and US$80, respectively, for December 2026 and to US$80 and US$75, respectively, for 2027, reflecting its new assumption that Middle East shipping disruptions will continue into 2027.
In the product market, global diesel supply will remain tight due to a lack of spare refining capacity, Russia's ban on exports and the approach of peak winter demand, senior industry executives said on Tuesday.
Americans faced record-high gasoline prices over the Labor Day holiday weekend as continued attacks on refining infrastructure and new threats constrained global supply, keeping upward pressure on fuel prices, while US diesel prices also reached record highs last week.
"Refined-product markets could remain tighter than the crude market, particularly if refinery capacity and logistics remain constrained for an extended period," said Paolo Broccardo, CEO at BankPro.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak's Serian records very unhealthy API reading of 239
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today.
Data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System portal showed Serian recording the highest reading at 239, followed by Samarahan (219) and Sri Aman (215).
Another 19 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sarawak accounting for five of the readings.
Sarikei recorded the highest unhealthy reading at 184, followed by ILP Miri (174) and Bintulu (167).
The other
two Sarawak areas
with unhealthy readings were Miri (164) and Sibu (163).
Outside Sarawak, Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 165, while Shah Alam in Selangor recorded 163.
Tasek Ipoh in Perak and Nilai in Negri Sembilan each recorded 159, followed by Banting in Selangor (158), and Seri Manjung, Tanjung Malim and Putrajaya (156 each).
Other areas with unhealthy readings were Klang (155), Petaling Jaya (154), Pegoh Ipoh (152), Kuala Selangor (151), Alor Gajah (144) and Bukit Rambai (130).
Meanwhile, 31 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while three stations recorded good air quality.
Kangar recorded an API reading of 45, followed by Balik Pulau in Penang (43) and Langkawi in Kedah (22).
Under the API classification, readings between 101 and 200 are considered unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are classified as very unhealthy.
Readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.
The United Nations has warned that a very strong El Niño is developing and could intensify in the coming months, raising the risk of extreme weather into 2027.

Title: Prasarana Integreated appoints Theta Edge's unit as network operator, strategic partner for Shah Alam line
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Theta Telecoms Sdn Bhd (TTEL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Theta Edge Bhd, has been appointed as the network operator and strategic partner for the development of a telecommunications common network infrastructure along the Shah Alam Line right of way.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Theta Edge said TTEL accepted a letter of acceptance for the project on Sept 7, 2026, from Prasarana Integrated Development Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Prasarana Malaysia Bhd.
"The scope of the services includes network design and engineering, civil works and fibre optic cable installation, integration with existing commercial fibre optic networks, and network equipment installation," it said.
Theta Edge said TTEL's appointment as a strategic partner will generate additional income for Prasarana Integrated in the technology services space through monetising the Shah Alam line right of way along tracks, stations, developments, and other locations.
The company said TTEL will also generate income by providing network telecommunication services by leveraging the Shah Alam line right of way granted.
"By providing value-added services by leveraging the underlying network telecommunication infrastructure, the enterprise market, and the employer's customer base and brand," it said.
Theta Edge said the contract period shall comprise an initial period of five years commencing Sept 1, 2026.
It said Prasarana Integrated is entitled to a minimum of RM500,000 per annum or 13 per cent of the project's gross revenue throughout the contract period, while the remaining balance of the revenue will be under TTEL.
"The project represents an opportunity for the company to leverage its existing expertise and venture into a recurring income-generating project to ensure a steady stream of revenue and cash flow in the future and ride on the future data demand growth in the area," Theta Edge added.
