Title: Malaysia’s SMART team arrives in Nepal disaster zone, begins drone reconnaissance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The  Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) arrived in Dhunche, Nepal, today to establish a forward base and begin aerial reconnaissance operations using drones in the disaster-stricken area.
According to a statement issued by the Home-Based Support Team (HBST) of MAS01 SMART, under the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), the 10-member team, led by Inspector Abdullah Ahmad Sobri, travelled to the location aboard an MI-17 helicopter.
It said the team departed from the Nepal Army Tactical Headquarters in Trishuli at 1 pm Malaysian time and arrived in Dhunche about 45 minutes later.
“Dhunche serves as the tactical forward base for managing disaster operations in the Rasuwa area, covering Timure, Syafrubesi, Dhunche and Mailung.
“Upon arrival, the SMART team established a forward base to serve as a staging area and temporary accommodation should operational conditions require it,” the statement said.
The statement said today’s operational planning focused on drone reconnaissance activities, which were divided into two groups covering four sectors between Syafrubesi and Timure.
However, the joint operation involving SMART personnel and the Nepalese Army faced challenges due to almost daily rainfall, which hampered drone flight operations in the field.
As a result, the SMART team is continuously evaluating the most suitable methods to ensure optimal aerial image data collection, which will subsequently be analysed to support further operational planning.
The MAS01 SMART team, deployed as part of the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission, arrived in Kathmandu last Saturday aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft.
The team also brought 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue (SAR) equipment, including high-capacity drones, communication systems and tunnel rescue equipment, to support operations in the flood-stricken country. — Bernama

Title: Dzulkefly: Status of five aboard Flying Doctor Service helicopter still unknown after Sarawak crash
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 8 — The status of five people aboard a Health Ministry (MOH) Flying Doctor Service helicopter that crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) airport in Sarawak this afternoon remains unknown, as search and rescue operations continue.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the helicopter, which departed from Miri, was carrying a pilot and four MOH health personnel — a medical officer, medical assistant and two nurses — who were on official duty.
“Based on the initial information received, the flight that departed from Miri was operated by one pilot and carried four MOH health personnel, namely one medical officer, one medical assistant and two nurses who were on official duty,” he said in a statement.
Dzulkefly said the status of all crew members and passengers, as well as the cause of the incident, had yet to be confirmed.
Search and rescue (SAR) teams, together with medical personnel and the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), were at the scene near the Long Lellang STOLport and the operation was ongoing.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) earlier said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
CAAM said the BO-105 helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot.
It did not provide details on the condition of those on board.
Dzulkefly said MOH was closely monitoring the situation and working with security authorities, rescue teams and relevant aviation agencies to obtain accurate and updated information from the scene.
The ministry was also in the process of contacting the next-of-kin and family members of those involved to provide the necessary support, he said.
“As the SAR operation is still ongoing, I urge the media and members of the public not to speculate or disseminate unverified information out of respect for the feelings of the victims’ families.
“Any further developments will be announced from time to time after receiving official confirmation from the authorities,” he said.
CAAM said earlier that the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the Transport Ministry would investigate the incident in accordance with Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.
The Flying Doctor Service provides medical services to communities in remote areas that are difficult to access, including parts of Sarawak. The service has operated in Sarawak since 1973.
“Let us pray that the search and rescue operation will be facilitated and proceed smoothly,” Dzulkefly said.

Title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300m deal
Article:
LONDON, Sept 8 — Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced today.
No fee was disclosed by the club, but the BBC reported that the five-year deal was worth £300 million (RM1.6 billion) in total.
A contract worth more than £60 million a season, would represent an increase on the current £50 million-per-season deal with retail bank Standard Chartered, who have been the Reds’ front-of-shirt sponsor since 2010.
Liverpool’s new deal is believed to be the most lucrative purely front-of-shirt agreement in Premier League history, with Arsenal and Manchester City’s agreements with Emirates and Etihad Airways respectively also involving stadium naming rights.
By contrast, six-time European champions Liverpool’s home ground is still solely known by its original name of Anfield.
In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League.
Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.
Standard Chartered will remain as the shirt sponsor this season before becoming a “global partner” of Liverpool from 2027/28 onwards.
It is understood that talks with Turkish Airlines started before 1892 Holdings — a consortium led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia, the Liverpool vice-chairman, purchased a stake of around 38 percent in the club last month.
Chief commercial officer Ben Latty said that the front of the shirt “holds a special place in the history” of Liverpool, adding that the partnership will build on “strong foundations” from the club’s Champions League final win in the Turkish city of Istanbul in 2005.
Turkish Airlines chief executive Ahmet Olmustur said: “This partnership brings together two global brands united by their international reach, commitment to excellence and ability to inspire millions of people around the world.”
Turkey’s national flag carrier boasts that it flies to 356 destinations in 132 countries. A pet soft-power project of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the company is controlled by the country’s wealth fund, which owns 49.1 percent of its shares.
The company’s network centres on Istanbul airport, which overtook London Heathrow as Europe’s busiest airport in the July summer peak with more than eight million travellers. — AFP

Title: Former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez to be charged tomorrow over RCI-linked probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
A check of the court system showed that Abdul Azeez, a former Baling MP, is scheduled to be charged before Judge Azura Alwi at 9 am.
On Aug 27, the former TH chairman and former Treasury secretary-general were each remanded for seven days, until Sept 2, to assist investigations following disclosures related to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
Both individuals are being investigated under Section 23(1) of the MACC Act 2009.
The RCI report on TH, published on the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) official portal on July 29, recommended, among other measures, a forensic audit to examine past investment decision-making that led to a significant decline in the institution’s asset value.
The RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, also identified investments requiring a forensic audit.
The report also found suspicious transactions and concealed information.
The RCI investigated issues involving TH, drawing on findings by PricewaterhouseCoopers, Ernst & Young, and Roland Berger, but did not cover the restructuring and recovery plans being implemented at the time. — Bernama

Title: Flying Doctor Service helicopter carrying five crashes near Long Lellang airport
Article:
KUCHING, 8 Sept — A BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) airport, about 929 kilometres north of Kuching, today.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm.
The helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot, CAAM said in a statement.
CAAM, however, did not mention any casualties in its statement.
“The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), under the Transport Ministry, will investigate the incident in accordance with Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: MACC: Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties, ensure independent enforcement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties for political parties that breach contribution limits or fail to report their funding, while also establishing an independent regulatory body to ensure the law is effectively enforced.
Deputy director of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the matter is among five key governance principles to consider when drafting the Bill.
He said the five principles comprised transparency, accountability, equity and fairness, independence, and inclusiveness and participation.
“Under the principle of accountability, there should be clear penalties for breaching contribution limits or failing to report funding, as well as, of course, a responsible regulatory body.
“The regulatory body has yet to be decided. There have been suggestions that the role could be given to the Election Commission (EC), the MACC, or a newly established special commission,” he said.
He said this while speaking as a panellist at the Political Financing Reform Forum: Balancing Transparency, Accountability and Democratic Participation, organised by the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department, here today.
Mohd Gunawan said the matter is still open to further review, with BHEUU to determine the most suitable proposal before bringing it to Parliament.
On the principle of equity and fairness, he said contribution limits and conditional public funding are important to ensure that political parties, whether small or large, compete on a more transparent, level playing field while strengthening democracy.
Meanwhile, he said the regulatory body must be independent and free from interference by any party, including the ruling party or external interests.
“This regulatory body has a significant responsibility to ensure that the law is properly and effectively enforced,” he said.
On the principle of inclusiveness and participation, Mohd Gunawan said the law-drafting process should provide the widest possible opportunity for civil society, stakeholders and political parties to give their views.
He said political parties are among the most important stakeholders in implementing the law and should be involved in developing comprehensive legislation that reflects its intended purpose.
“We need to ensure that this does not restrict democracy itself, but instead helps to strengthen democratic participation in a democratic country,” he said.
Mohd Gunawan said the Political Financing Bill is also needed to close gaps in existing laws, including the Societies Act 1966 and the Election Offences Act 1954.
He said greater transparency in political financing is expected to increase public trust in the country’s system and governance, as well as strengthen Malaysia’s standing internationally. — Bernama

Title: Zaid urges Putrajaya to safeguard Petronas interests in Sarawak talks
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to ensure the federal government and Petronas’ interests are protected as Putrajaya continues negotiations with Sarawak over the state’s oil and gas rights.
His comments come ahead of a meeting on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), which Anwar is expected to chair in Kota Kinabalu on Friday.
In a post on X, Zaid expressed concern that political considerations could influence the government’s handling of Sarawak’s demands, particularly over Petros’ role as the state’s sole gas aggregator.
He said Putrajaya should ensure that decisions involving the country’s oil and gas resources were made transparently and with the wider national interest in mind.
“Anwar must not exchange political support for oil and gas to Sarawak,” he said.
Zaid also questioned whether Petros’ position as Sarawak’s sole gas aggregator would be further strengthened following the meeting, claiming the role could be worth RM10 billion annually.
He pointed to Sarawak’s previous success in imposing its state sales tax on petroleum products, which he said had brought the state billions of ringgit in revenue.
Let the courts settle legal dispute, says Zaid
Zaid, who recently joined PAS, said disagreements over the respective legal rights of Sarawak and Petronas should ultimately be determined through the courts rather than political negotiations.
“Let the Federal Court decide; let the rights of Petronas be litigated,” he said.
The former minister said discussions surrounding MA63 should be conducted openly and should balance Sarawak’s constitutional rights with the interests of the federation as a whole.
He also called on opposition parties and Umno leaders to state their positions on the dispute, questioning whether political parties were reluctant to speak out because of the influence East Malaysian parties wield in determining who commands a parliamentary majority.
Sarawak and Petronas have been locked in negotiations over the state’s oil and gas regulatory framework and Petros’ role in the gas sector.
The dispute has raised broader questions over the relationship between federal petroleum laws, Sarawak’s state legislation and the rights arising from MA63.

Title: Johor orders hunt for five feral dogs after girl mauled in Batu Pahat
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — The Johor government has directed a large-scale operation to hunt and capture five feral dogs that attacked a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak in Batu Pahat last weekend.
Johor religious committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said efforts are being carried out by the Batu Pahat district office in collaboration with the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police.
He said the operation will be intensified for at least a week with deployment of various methods to ensure the detection of the dogs and their eventual capture.
“The methods would use a host of techniques that include monitoring and surveillance operations that is permitted under the law.
“Our commitment is to overcome the feral and stray dog problem in the area to ensure that similar incidents do not happen to others,” he told reporters during a visiting Nur Haira Wafiqah Muhammad Hamizi who is currently receiving treatment at the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) of the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) here today.
Last Saturday, Nur Haira was found covered in blood with head and facial injuries after being mauled by a group of five feral dogs.
She was later rushed to hospital for medical treatment to her injuries.
Mohd Fared said the immediate capture of the feral animals involved needs to be carried out to ensure that they are free of rabies.
He said this was important not only to ensure public safety, but to also reduce concerns on Nur Haira’s long-term health.
“So this requires immediate action so that the feral and stray dogs in the area can be checked and examined for rabies,” he said, adding that priority is to ensure the child’s recovery.
Mohd Fared, who is also the Semerah assemblyman, said the state government is fully committed to cover Nur Haira’s medical and rehabilitation costs as she is expected to undergo a lengthy recovery.
He also called on the relevant authorities to look into Nur Haira family’s mental trauma and  psychological well-being.
Mohd Fared said that priority to the incident, the Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) together with DVS had carried out operations on August 12, 26 and 30 where they successfully captured 22 stray dogs in the area.
Despite this, he said the number of stray and feral dogs still roaming in the area showed that continuous efforts are needed.

Title: Johari: Parliamentary Service Act gives Parliament greater scope to strengthen oversight of government
Article:
CAMERON HIGHLANDS, Sept 8 — The implementation of the Parliamentary Service Act (PSA) provides Parliament with the scope to streamline its legislative role, including strengthening special select committees to assist the government in identifying shortcomings and addressing public issues, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.
He said the enactment of the PSA created a new environment after Parliament operated under executive oversight for 33 years, enabling the legislative body to play a more independent role in contributing to national prosperity.
He said under the 10 ministry-related committees established, each is comprised of 12 Members of Parliament (MPs) representing both government and opposition backbenchers who do not hold ministerial or deputy ministerial posts.
“They have broad terms of reference and powers under the Standing Orders to summon any party for hearings on issues concerning the public or shortcomings in ministerial execution.
“These committees will produce reports and recommendations that can subsequently be debated in the Dewan Rakyat, ensuring their views and proposals receive serious attention from the executive,” he said.
He said this at a press conference following the opening of the Conference of Speakers of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies 2026 by Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail here today.
Johari said this approach allowed any oversights or issues at the ministerial level to be identified early before escalating into larger problems.
He noted that previously, major decisions were predominantly made by the executive, and any operational flaws could lead to prolonged complications.
He added that the PSA also facilitated Parliament in planning and implementing reforms, as legislative-related decisions were now made by the Speaker and Parliament, with the minister in charge of law and parliamentary affairs acting as a coordinator.
Meanwhile, Johari said the conference served as a platform to share best practices between the Malaysian Parliament and state legislative assemblies to strengthen federal-state legislative ties based on the principles of federalism.
He said the conference provided an avenue to deliberate on enhancement proposals and produce resolutions to guide legislative institutions in the future.
Among the areas that could be strengthened, he said, was bringing the legislature closer to the public, including creating more opportunities for citizens and students to engage with Parliament and state assemblies. — Bernama

Title: Brothers get High Court leave to challenge DBKL approval for 39-storey towers near their Old Klang Road home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Two brothers have obtained High Court permission to challenge Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s approval for two 39-storey residential towers planned less than 11 metres from their home along Jalan Klang Lama.
The Edge
reported that Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad granted T Kanagarasah, 38, and T Mahendra Kumar, 42, leave to seek judicial review of the project, with the Attorney General’s Chambers not opposing the application.
The judge also granted an interim stay on the development until the brothers’ application for a permanent stay is heard on October 8, despite an objection from the Attorney General’s Chambers.
The brothers are seeking to overturn a development order issued on January 20 and a building plan approved on March 10 for the two towers and a hawker centre on three lots in Mukim Petaling.
The proposed project is expected to have 1,544 residential units, with the brothers also seeking general damages and costs.
In his supporting affidavit, Kanagarasah said their home, which is 69 years old, was less than 11 metres from the proposed development and that the brothers were shown the project’s development order and building plan on March 6.
He said they were unable to attend a public hearing to object to the project but had submitted a written objection that same day.
Among their concerns was the expected increase in traffic, with Kanagarasah claiming that more than 1,500 new homes could bring an additional 2,000 to 3,000 vehicles into the area.
He also raised concerns about construction-related noise and dust, potential flooding and the impact on surrounding residents’ privacy and the area’s already high density.
The brothers later submitted another objection, alleging that no environmental impact assessment had been conducted for the project and that the development order was inconsistent with the Kuala Lumpur Structure Plan.
They further claimed City Hall’s approval was unlawful, including in relation to requirements for notifying adjoining landowners under the relevant planning laws.
The brothers initially filed the judicial review application through Messrs Peters Chambers on June 6 before appointing Messrs Cheow Wee and Mai as their new solicitors on September 5.
The Edge
confirmed the court’s decision with lawyer Cheow Wee.

Title: MetMalaysia: Anak Krakatau ash could reach Malaysia, but risk remains low
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The risk of volcanic ash from Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is currently low, although changes in wind direction and speed as well as possible further eruptions could affect its movement, MetMalaysia said today.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said current wind conditions and monitoring of the ash showed that the plume was mainly concentrated around the Sunda Strait and nearby areas of Indonesia, BuletinTV3 reported.
“MetMalaysia will continue to monitor the situation using satellite data and atmospheric analysis.
“Information from global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centres (VAACs) also allows any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace to be identified and communicated to the public promptly,” he said.
Earlier, media reports said continued eruptions from Anak Krakatau since Friday had spread volcanic ash and prompted six airports to suspend flight operations.
The disruption also affected domestic and international flights, including routes linking Jakarta with Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul/Incheon, Doha and Amsterdam.
On the potential impact if the ash reaches Malaysia, Mohd Hisham said the biggest concern would be disruption to domestic and international flight operations.
He said volcanic eruptions were monitored by VAACs under the supervision of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).
“If the information received indicates a potential impact on Malaysian airspace, MetMalaysia will issue volcanic ash threat warnings or advisories to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), airline operators and airport operators,” he said.
Mohd Hisham also clarified that the reduced visibility currently experienced, particularly in Sarawak and parts of the western peninsula, was caused by transboundary haze and not volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau.

Title: AI-powered traffic centre launched to boost safety, speed up response on three Klang Valley highways
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — With rising traffic volumes and frequent incidents putting greater pressure on highway operators, a new smart traffic control centre covering three major Klang Valley highways was launched today to enhance road safety and enable faster responses through real-time monitoring.
The centre will oversee operations along the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE) and Kajang-Seremban Highway (LEKAS), all managed by IJM Corporation Berhad.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said past data showed that 85.4 per cent of traffic accidents on tolled expressways last year were attributed to human factors, while the remainder involved vehicle and environmental factors.
He said his ministry, together with the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), was committed to further strengthening the development of smart expressways to provide users with a safer and more seamless journey experience.
“Based on data from the Malaysian Highway Road Accident Database System (MHROADS), a total of 26,675 traffic accidents were recorded on tolled expressways in 2025, including 839 fatality cases.
“With the increase in vehicles and growing user needs, our expressways need to evolve from physical infrastructure into smart mobility ecosystems that are safer, smarter and more efficient,” he said in his speech at the control centre’s officiating ceremony at the BESRAYA Loke Yew Toll Plaza here.
With more than six million vehicles using Peninsular Malaysia’s expressway network daily, Nanta said the federal government, through the Works Ministry, was committed to expediting the implementation of the Intelligent Transport System (ITS) under the Malaysia ITS Roadmap 2030.
Among the key elements of the roadmap is the adoption of smart mobility solutions that leverage real-time data analytics to optimise traffic management and user experience.
At present, LLM’s Traffic Management Centre conducts round-the-clock traffic surveillance through 873 integrated closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras and 278 variable message signs (VMS), enabling earlier incident detection and the timely dissemination of information to road users while expediting response efforts and traffic flow recovery.
Meanwhile, IJM’s AI-powered smart expressway traffic control centre integrates 144 CCTV cameras, 87 Video Incident Detection System units, 35 Automatic Number Plate Recognition units and 22 VMS units for the three aforementioned expressways.
Nanta said transforming existing expressways into smart highways was a collective responsibility involving the ministry, concessionaires, enforcement agencies, emergency responders and technology providers.
He then urged other highway concessionaires to adopt a similar approach in their traffic management operations to improve incident detection and enable a more effective and streamlined response.
“The use of technology does not necessarily mean replacing human labour; instead, it should serve as a catalyst for increased productivity and the creation of new employment opportunities requiring specialised skills.
“Our goal is clear in ensuring that the technology integrated can tangibly benefit the people, particularly in terms of safety, efficiency and overall journey experience,” he said, adding that IJM had assured him its latest move would not result in any displacement of its existing workforce.
Separately, a road safety programme using virtual reality (VR) technology was also launched to raise awareness among school students.
IJM Group chief executive and managing director Datuk Lee Chun Fai said the programme was part of a collaboration between LLM and the Royal Malaysia Police to promote safer motorcycle riding habits among students.
“The VR programme is targeted at school students, as 80 per cent of fatalities involve motorcyclists,” he said.

Title: MetMalaysia: Malaysia could see temperatures hit 40°C from January to May 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the likelihood of the phenomenon occurring was now approaching 100 per cent, based on climate model forecasts from international observation and research centres, according to a report published by
Berita Harian
.
He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country.
“Experience from the Super El Nino episodes of 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 showed that the country’s daily maximum temperatures at the time were more extreme than during other periods.
“The country recorded its highest temperature of 40.1°C at the Chuping Meteorological Station in Perlis on April 9, 1998, and 39.3°C at the Batu Embun Meteorological Station in Jerantut, Pahang on April 10, 2016,” he said.
Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.
“The situation could cause northern and inland areas of the peninsula, as well as inland Sabah and Sarawak, to record higher-than-usual temperatures and increase the risk of hot weather and heatwaves from the end of the North-east Monsoon in January until May 2027.
“Based on the latest projections, more meteorological stations in the northern peninsula could record temperatures of up to 40°C during the peak of the hot season between January and May 2027,” he said.
He warned that rising temperatures and prolonged hot weather could increase the risk of heatwaves and affect health, particularly among children, the elderly and those engaging in outdoor activities.
“Reduced rainfall and longer dry periods could put pressure on water resources, including catchment areas and dams, while also affecting agriculture and other industries sensitive to water shortages.
“Prolonged hot and dry conditions would also make vegetation more susceptible to fires, increasing the risk of forest and peatland fires as well as haze, both locally and across borders,” he said.

Title: Senior medical officer in Melaka remanded over RM1.5m knee implant supply probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 —  A senior medical officer has been remanded for five days to assist a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million.
The remand order for the man, in his 50s, was issued by Ayer Keroh Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman at the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court in Melaka this morning,
Harian Metro
reported.
The public servant has been remanded until September 12 after MACC applied for the order to facilitate further investigations.
According to a source, the suspect was detained at about 3.30pm yesterday after he arrived at the Melaka MACC office to give a statement.
The source said preliminary investigations found that the suspect was believed to have committed the alleged offence between 2024 and 2026.

Title: Anwar to chair MA63 meeting on Sabah’s 40pc revenue claim, says Hajiji
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Sabah’s claim for 40 per cent of its net revenue will be among the issues discussed at a Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) meeting to be chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim this Friday.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today.
Hajiji said the Sabah government was grateful to Anwar, as nine matters under MA63 had been resolved during his administration, including the devolution of certain powers to Sabah.
“Previously there were four matters, so a total of 13 (matters) have been resolved. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
Hajiji said the federal government had agreed to Sabah’s claim for the 40 per cent payment, but several technical issues remained to be resolved.
“They have agreed but there are still some issues, perhaps technical issues, that have been raised. This is a normal process because there is an appeal process, but it does not affect the decision for us to receive the 40 per cent payment,” he said.
He said unresolved matters would be raised again for consideration at subsequent MA63 meetings or negotiations.
In a separate development, Hajiji welcomed progress on the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant, which is nearing completion and is expected to begin producing vitamin E before the end of the year.
He said the plant represented a positive development and a downstream business for Sawit Kinabalu Group, using palm-based materials in its production.
“I am very pleased to hear the briefing from Sawit Kinabalu and the company working with Sawit Kinabalu that the plant built to produce vitamin E is almost completed and will produce vitamin E before the end of the year,” he said.
Hajiji said the project was believed to be the first of its kind in Malaysia and could help increase revenue for Sawit Kinabalu and its partner company.

Title: Former minister released on MACC bail over Tabung Haji RCI probe, chief commissioner confirms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — A former minister who was remanded over an investigation linked to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail today.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the release,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
“He (the former minister) has been released on MACC bail,” he said today.
The man, in his 60s, was initially remanded for five days from September 2 to 6 before his remand was extended by another two days until today.
The former lawmaker was detained after he appeared at the MACC headquarters here on September 2 to give a statement and was investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The RCI report, which was made public on July 29, contained 25 key recommendations aimed at improving transparency, professionalism and governance at the institution.
Among the recommendations was a proposal to bar active politicians from serving on the TH board to prevent political interference.
Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim had also called for investigations into the findings of the TH RCI to be pursued “to the ends of the earth”.

Title: Should political parties’ donors be protected? Azalina says issue among those being studied
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money?
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia.
Azalina today listed nine parameters or areas of the proposed political financing law that are currently being fine-tuned, including who the law will cover; the supervisory body; the source and limits of donations; prohibition on foreign donations; traceable ways of receiving funds; reporting, auditing and disclosure; and offences and penalties.
At a press conference here, Azalina gave examples of issues that still have to be considered under the proposed law, including foreign donors.
Azalina said some countries, for example, prohibit foreigners from donating, while others have procedures requiring foreign donors to disclose their donations.
“Secondly, when you donate, will you be subjected to income tax deduction, or you must inform the source of your money? If everyone who donates have to inform the source of the money, maybe many will not want to donate,” she said at a press conference after the Political Financing Convention 2026.
Noting that some people might donate to all political parties as a form of “buying insurance”, Azalina said another issue to be considered was whether the law would allow donors to contribute to more than one political party.
She added that there was a possibility that no one would want to donate to political parties if such a law were introduced.
“And fourthly, do we want to make sure that when people donate, MACC won’t come and disturb, ‘why you donate?’” she said.
Later, when speaking on the same point, Azalina said she personally felt that political parties could issue receipts to donors, but said it had to be studied whether “to give protection to donors”, as donors might be deterred from donating if they were pursued after making donations.
“But we must give protection to donors also. If not, who will want to donate right?” she said at another point.
“But I agree if it’s a foreign donor, we must have a certain process. There must be a procedure, whether select committee or Parliament is informed, because if a foreign donor wants to influence our decision, this is also a problem right,” she said.
Azalina had explained that the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) had been carrying out engagement studies and surveys over the past two years.
Azalina today urged BHEUU to obtain written official views from political parties on whether they agreed with having a political financing law in Malaysia.
After that, Azalina said the proposed law would be brought to the Cabinet for evaluation from multiple perspectives.
She told the media that the Cabinet would then decide on the final “format” of the technical aspects of the proposed law before the Bill is brought to Parliament to be voted on.
Earlier, when speaking as minister in a speech at the same convention, Azalina said the government’s goal was not just to enact laws, but to ensure they were truly effective and capable of being implemented.
She had spoken of the simple principle of being “transparent but practical, stern but fair, and accountability without curbing the legitimate democratic process”.
Today, Azalina, when giving her personal opinion as a lawyer and MP, said politicians could easily find themselves being charged with corruption if there is no political funding law in Malaysia to regulate donations to them.

Title: Nazir Razak, Musa Hitam say NEP fostered ‘tongkat culture’ among Malays
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that the two made the remarks at a forum titled “Remembering Tun Abdul Razak: Architect of Malaysia’s Development and Nation Building”, which discussed whether the NEP should be reviewed, replaced or remodelled.
Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”.
“We will be in serious trouble if we have to continue. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.
He said the policy should be reviewed, with greater emphasis placed on education and professional development instead of the distribution of shares and ownership.
“The NEP focused too much on the distribution of shares and ownership. And when you go down that path, all these ‘Ali Babas’ come up,” he said, referring to a culture of rent-seeking.
“I think we focused on the wrong theme in the execution of the NEP,” he added.
Nazir also questioned the practice of awarding contracts to Bumiputera businesses, particularly why politicians were allowed to choose the recipients.
“They (politicians) don’t want competition among Bumiputeras,” he said, adding that the lack of competition had weakened Bumiputera businesses.
Musa, who served as deputy prime minister from 1981 to 1986, said the policy had also made Malays overly reliant on government assistance.
“To me, the economic policy for the Malays has caused the Malays to become too pampered. Pampered by the government,” he said.
Musa said the NEP had benefited Malays and the country as a whole, but had also created a sense of insecurity, with recipients continuing to feel that government assistance was insufficient.
“People fear receiving nothing, but even when they receive assistance, they say it is not enough and ask for more.”

Title: Did the Negeri Sembilan MB sign decree to oust ruler? Claim sees state in renewed palace crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him.
According to
The Straits Times
, the explosive allegation was made public in a September 5 statement by the state’s four traditional ruling chieftains, the Undang Yang Empat, who possess customary authority under Adat Perpatih to elect and — they claim — dismiss the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
When pressed on the allegations on September 6, Ismail did not directly deny signing the decree, stating only that “the four Undang have the right to their opinion” while reaffirming that he “and the state government express full loyalty to Muhriz Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar”.
The standoff is the most recent escalation yet in a months-long palace conflict that could colour Malaysian politics ahead of key elections.
According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler.
The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.
Sources told
The Straits Times
that the private meeting was attended by top Umno leaders, including party president and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
All three reportedly declined requests for comment.
However, legal and government sources told
The Straits Times
that Ismail has privately claimed he was coerced into signing the document under severe political duress, alleging that Umno’s central leadership orchestrated the manoeuvre alongside the chieftains.
The same sources indicated that Ismail is preparing to lodge an official police report regarding the incident today.
Despite the purported signing on August 3, Ismail proceeded to swear in his state executive council before Tuanku Muhriz four days later on August 7, entrenching an extraordinary constitutional contradiction.
This development will again put the spotlight on Umno’s role in the Negeri Sembilan constitutional crisis.
Ahead of last month’s state election, Umno’s state lawmakers had withdrawn support for the menteri besar at the time, Datuk Seri Aminudin Harun, ostensibly for his public support of Tuanku Muhriz in the public row with the four Undang, before suddenly reversing this position.
Umno had sought to mitigate this prior to the election by positioning itself as a “mediator” to resolve the royal crisis.
“This is about crisis management. It’s how you manage the crisis. That is why the rakyat must consider all factors before they decide,” said Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, one of the key personalities in the move to oust Aminudin

Title: Fahmi: Govt agencies to work together to tighten e-commerce rules, curb sale of prohibited goods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said such cooperation was important as there were still gaps in the country’s e-commerce ecosystem, particularly as e-commerce platforms are currently not subject to licensing.
“There are indeed gaps in the e-commerce system. At present, e-commerce is not yet licensed, so we need to look into this matter,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the Huawei WAIC Connect Malaysia 2026 Symposium today.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had held a meeting with a major platform yesterday, but he had yet to receive an update on the outcome of the meeting as of this morning.
He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered.
“The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.
Fahmi stressed that platforms needed to address the issue of fake accounts being created and the sale of prohibited products, rather than merely removing search keywords, which could make such products harder to find without addressing the actual problem.
“That should not be the way,” he said, adding that platforms needed to prevent fake accounts from being created for the purpose of selling drugs.
Previously, MCMC was instructed to hold meetings with e-commerce platforms following concerns over the online sale of drugs, including fentanyl and a substance referred to as “piu-piu”.
Fahmi said he had received a message from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim regarding the phenomenon, which was seen as increasingly worrying. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Malaysians want political funding law before GE16; political parties’ buy-in needed to avoid delay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
Azalina’s remarks were based on findings from the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) public engagement sessions.
“I was informed by the BHEUU deputy director general (policy) many voices of the public wants, if possible, that this Act can be in force before the 16th general election,” she said at the Political Financing Convention 2026 held at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) building.
Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law.
“So they are the users and they will vote on the law. So you must have them to have more say. If not, the delay of the Act may happen if there is no buy-in from political parties,” she said.
Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the enactment of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.
“And certainly the people have the right to hope for changes and to demand the government fulfill the commitment as soon as possible.
“But on behalf of the government, I admit that the agenda of institutional legal reform, when we talk about political financing, is not a process that is that simple and capable of being implemented so quickly,” she said, emphasising the need for political parties to be stakeholders and to give their views since the proposed law would apply to them.
“Political will is not just measured by how quickly a reform is presented, but it also has to be evaluated based on the courage to start it, the readiness to accept views and criticism, and the strength of determination to carry it out,” she added.
Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the enactment of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.
Azalina noted that BHEUU had carried out engagement work on the proposed law reform over the past two years.
Later at a press conference, Azalina replied to a question on why the political financing law had yet to be introduced in Malaysia, saying this was due to studies being carried out over the past two years: “The delay is not a political delay, but delay in terms of process and procedure done by BHEUU.”
Asked if it was possible for the proposed political financing law to be introduced before GE16, Azalina said the question of when GE16 would be held should be directed to the prime minister.
As for the timeline for how soon the law could be introduced, Azalina said, “I wish it’s as soon as possible”, but that it would depend on the work being done to prepare the Bill.
At the press conference, Azalina outlined various technical aspects of the proposed political financing law that have to be considered before it is brought to the Cabinet, and also proposed that BHEUU collect the written official opinions of all registered political parties in Malaysia on whether they agree to such a law.
Findings show 90.3 per cent want political financing law before GE16
Earlier at the convention, BHEUU deputy director-general (policy and development) Datuk Punitha Silivarajoo presented the findings from BHEUU’s engagement involving 1,544 participants nationwide in 12 engagement sessions from June to November 2025.
Punitha said 100 per cent of the 1,544 participants agreed that Malaysia needs to have a political financing law, and that 90.3 per cent of the 1,544 wanted this law to be tabled and passed in Parliament before the next general election.
Out of the 1,544 participants, 67 per cent were political parties and grassroots leaders, 17 per cent were government agencies and academics, 11 per cent were non-governmental organisations (NGOs), civil society organisations (CSOs) and youths, and five per cent were from the business sector.
A total of 32 political parties and 69 NGOs and CSOs were consulted in the engagement sessions with 1,544 participants.
Separately, BHEUU also commissioned the International Islamic University Malaysia to conduct a study on public perception on the proposal for a political financing law, with the research team also including researchers from Universiti Malaya, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Universiti Malaysia Sabah, the Bar Council, Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs, and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4).
The public perception study involved 3,422 survey respondents, 11 focus group discussions involving 103 participants, and in-depth interviews with 14 individuals with the necessary expertise and influence in the political landscape; with the final report totalling 708 pages completed in February this year.

Title: Lim Guan Eng hits PAS over failure to credit him for cutting lottery draws from 22 to eight a year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at PAS over what he described as dishonest and hypocritical claims about DAP’s position on Islam, while pointing to his record of reducing special lottery draws when he was finance minister.
In a Facebook post, Lim said PAS had failed to acknowledge that he was the first finance minister to reduce the number of special lottery draws from 22 to eight a year when Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in government from 2018 to 2020.
“PAS is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year during the PH government from 2018 to 2020,” he said.
Lim said the number of special draws was subsequently increased to 22 a year by the PAS, Umno, Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) coalition government in 2020 and remained at that level until the BN/PN administration ended in late 2022.
He said PAS did not have to praise him for the policy, but questioned its repeated claims that DAP leaders were opposed to Islam.
“Not praising me is fine, but the question is why does PAS like to slander DAP leaders as being against Islam when DAP is only opposed to PAS and their politics of hatred and lies,” he said.
Lim said it was up to the public to decide whether PAS’ approach amounted to hypocrisy and violated its own principles.
“It is up to the people to determine whether PAS’ two-faced political game violates principles and is hypocritical,” he said.

Title: IBS classrooms to ease overcrowding in Melaka schools, says deputy education minister
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 8 — The construction of additional classrooms using the Industrialised Building System (IBS) will enable special rooms currently used as temporary teaching and learning spaces to resume their original functions, said Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh.
He said the move would help ease overcrowding while enabling schools to make better use of their existing facilities.
“Some schools have had to convert special rooms, including music rooms and laboratories, into classrooms.
“With this construction, the special rooms can once again be used for their intended purposes,” he told reporters after visiting Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Taman Merdeka here today.
According to Wong, 53 schools in Melaka had benefited from the construction of additional classrooms using IBS, 49 of which had more than 35 students per class.
He said three schools in the Kesidang state constituency, namely SK Malim, SK Taman Merdeka and SK Tengkera 1, had received a total allocation of RM3.3 million to construct 11 additional classrooms under the initiative, with completion expected by December 2026.
“The additional classroom construction projects at the three schools are currently around 40 per cent complete and are expected to be completed before the 2027 school session begins,” he said.
Commenting on the double-cohort intake for Year One in the 2027 school session, Wong said 416,632 pupils had so far registered in the seven-year-old cohort, while 73,487 had registered in the six-year-old cohort.
On teacher readiness, he said the Ministry of Education (MOE) had taken several measures, including placing Institute of Teacher Education (IPG) graduates this year, appointing reserve candidates for critical options and recruiting teachers on a Contract of Service (COS) basis.
“A total of 3,150 people have already been appointed and are ready for placement in schools according to future needs,” he said.
On the haze issue, Wong said the MOE has clear guidelines on school activities based on the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading.
He said all outdoor activities would be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, while schools would be closed and online learning implemented if it exceeds 200.
“However, the MOE also takes into account parents’ concerns about their children’s health. If parents are still worried, they can choose not to send their children to school. That is the parents’ choice,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Blocked trails delayed six hikers’ return from Gunung Gerah, says Perak Fire Dept
Article:
GERIK, 8 Sept — The closure and obstruction of hiking trails that have not been used for a long time were the main reasons why the six hikers took a longer time to make their way before they were found safe last night, after participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, on August 29.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the hikers found that the trails at Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat were closed due to these factors.
“When they reached Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat, the found that the trails to both these hills were closed as they had not been used by hikers for a long time.
“Due to the difficulties faced, such as fallen trees, it resulted in them taking a longer time (to make their way out),” she said when met at Jeti Trojan, Tasik Banding, here today.
She said the hiking area’s lack of communication coverage also contributed to the loss of contact, thereby sparking concerns among the victims’ families before a police report was lodged.
The victims, she said, managed to reach Bukit Bongok and obtained a mobile phone signal to contact their families, enabling their exact location to be determined and for them to be safely rescued.
Earlier, the six hikers safely made their way out of Pos Kemar at 10.20am today via Jeti Trojan here.
The six — Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39; his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39; their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9; as well mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43 — were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.
Previously, the six were reported missing after they went hiking at the mountain on August 29 and failed to exit the forest by the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members lodged a police report on Sunday (September 6). — Bernama

Title: AirAsia resumes most flights disrupted by Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — AirAsia has resumed flights to and from destinations affected by the Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption following the reopening of Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
The airline said the airport had been temporarily closed since September 6 due to volcanic ash clouds from the eruption which posed a significant threat to safe aircraft operations in the vicinity of volcanic clouds.
“With Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport now reopened following its temporary closure since September 6, 2026, AirAsia has resumed affected services to and from Jakarta, with the exception of two flights on September 8, 2026,” it said in a statement today.
The two affected flights are QZ178 from Jakarta (CGK) to Bandar Lampung (TKG) and QZ179 from Bandar Lampung to Jakarta.
AirAsia said all affected guests had been notified of their flight status and recovery options, adding that it is working to ensure passengers could resume their journeys safely on the next available flight.
It advised guests travelling to or from the affected destinations to check their latest flight status on its website at airasia.com/flightstatus, as the weather situation remains fluid. — Bernama

Title: Perak Fire Dept calls for age limits on children joining high-risk mountain expeditions
Article:
GERIK, Sept 8 — The Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) recommends that the authorities review the standard operating procedure (SOP) regarding the age limit for children participating in extreme activities and hiking expeditions along challenging routes in mountainous areas.
Perak JPBM director Datuk Sayani Saidon (she) said the measure should be given attention to reduce risks when conducting such high-risk activities.
“This recommendation is because the risk of physical injury for children who go through challenging tracks is higher than adult climbers.
“If there is no standard (SOP), I feel it is time for the relevant department to look at this matter more carefully and transparently so that we can limit the involvement of climbers, especially underage ones, for the safety factor itself,” she said when met at the Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding, here, today.
Previously, six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, were safely released from Pos Kemar, 10.20 this morning.
The six victims involved, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Post Health Clinic Kemar.
Previously, the six victims were reported missing after climbing the mountain on August 29, after reportedly failing to leave the forest on the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members filed a police report on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Police to record statements from six Gunung Gerah hikers after rescue
Article:
BAGAN SERAI, Sept 8 — Police will record statements from six hikers in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing during the hiking trip.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the six hikers would be taken to the Gerik District Police Headquarters (IPD) for documentation after being brought out from Pos Kemar.
“They will all be allowed to return home after the documentation process is completed. They are also reported to be in good health,” he said at a press conference at the Kerian IPD here today.
Asked whether the couple had committed an offence by bringing their two children on the hiking trip, Mohd Alwi said all four had valid permits.
“There was no issue (with the couple bringing their children along) as the permit included details of their family members,” he said.
Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, and their two children, Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, together with mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken to the Pos Kemar Health Clinic for medical examinations.
The search and rescue (SAR) team and the victims left Pos Kemar at 8.30am today and arrived at Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding, at 10.20am before proceeding to the Gerik IPD.
The six began their hike on August 29 and were due to emerge from the forest on September 3.
A report was lodged by their family members on Sunday after they failed to return as scheduled. — Bernama

Title: Six Gunung Gerah hikers safely out of forest after days missing
Article:
IPOH, Sept 8 — Six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, have safely left Pos Kemar this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, left Pos Kemar at 8.30 this morning and arrived at Trojan Jetty, Tasik Banding at 10.20am.
“All the victims and the SAR (search and rescue) team arrived safely at Pos Kemar at approximately 9.15pm last night. All the victims underwent a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic and rested at the facility.
“They were then taken to the Gerik IPD by police for documentation and further action,” he said in a statement here.
Previously, the six victims involved were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.
Earlier, the six victims were reported missing after climbing the mountain on August 29, after reportedly failing to leave the forest on the scheduled date, which was September 3, and family members filed a police report on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia plans 9GW of gas-fired power capacity by 2032 as demand rises, says economy minister
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Malaysia expects about nine gigawatts (GW) of gas-fired power capacity to be deployed by 2032 as the country manages growing electricity demand while progressively phasing out coal-fired generation.
Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the capacity would form part of the country’s efforts to manage electricity demand, with the last coal-fired power plant expected to be retired in 2044.
Akmal Nasrullah said energy demand was showing an upward trend, driven by factors including population growth and higher consumption from energy-intensive sectors such as data centres.
“In terms of the projection for energy demand, definitely we see a pattern of increase. One is population growth.
“But number two, there is also an increase in energy consumption by high-usage sectors such as data centres,” he told reporters after the Energy Regulatory Insights 2026 here today.
He said weather and climate conditions could also change energy demand patterns, particularly as hotter conditions increase the need for cooling systems and air conditioning.
Against this backdrop, Akmal Nasrullah said managing energy demand would become as crucial as managing energy supply over the next five to 10 years.
“I think for the next five to 10 years, Malaysia must really remain disciplined enough to ensure our system is continuously upgraded, not just in terms of the power produced, but also the grid and infrastructure, so that our system remains affordable, safe and sustainable,” he added.
He said energy planning should not only focus on the megawatts that need to be deployed in the system, but also on energy efficiency and conservation.
Akmal Nasrullah said the planning would need to be managed by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation and the Energy Commission to ensure the country could manage demand while remaining committed to sustainability efforts and reducing the energy sector’s carbon footprint.
Earlier in his keynote address, Akmal Nasrullah outlined three priorities for the next phase of energy reform, starting with the need for a competitive and progressive energy market with clear and predictable rules and transparent access arrangements.
Secondly, he said expanding generation capacity must be supported by a modern grid that is intelligent, visible, secure and flexible, with grid modernisation under the 13th Malaysia Plan regarded as essential economic infrastructure to enable investments to connect faster, improve system efficiency and support reliable economic growth.
Thirdly, Akmal Nasrullah said energy efficiency must be treated as an energy resource in its own right, as it could reduce operating costs, ease pressure on the system and strengthen competitiveness.
He said the first National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP) exceeded its original target, delivering cumulative electricity savings of 60,886 gigawatt-hours, equivalent to RM16.1 billion in savings, from 2016 to 2025.
Under NEEAP 2.0, Malaysia is targeting an 11.6 per cent reduction in energy demand against the business-as-usual scenario by 2035, which is expected to help lower energy costs, ease pressure on the system and support more productive and competitive economic activity. — Bernama

Title: Selangor on track to top RM100b investment mark this year, says Amirudin
Article:
SEPANG, Sept 8 — Selangor is confident that the value of investments recorded by the state this year will exceed RM100 billion based on the current positive momentum, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the state recorded about RM70 billion in investments up to mid-year, with the investment trend very encouraging.
“We set a target of RM80 billion, similar to the achievement in 2025, but by mid-2026, we had reached RM70 billion.
“Following this trend, we strongly believe we will be able to exceed the RM80 billion target. In fact, if the trend is very good, we are confident we can create a record of more than RM100 billion,” he said in a press conference after the delivery of vacant possession (VP) ceremony for the NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP) here today.
Amirudin said Selangor’s strong investment performance was also driven by the state government’s strategy of consistently carrying out investment missions abroad, including to France, Germany, Saudi Arabia and South Korea, showing that efforts to attract investment were being made extensively.
He said the development of new industrial areas, including NSIP in Sepang, as well as the development of a third port on Carey Island, is expected to continue to boost investment activities in Selangor.
“If the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) operates as scheduled at the end of this year and so on, I think this will all be exciting in several northern areas (and Selangor),” he said.
Regarding NSIP, Amirudin said more than 200 factories are expected to start operating after obtaining approvals, with most companies currently involved being local enterprises.
“This area is part of the Integrated Development Region in South Selangor (IDRISS), which was included in the First Selangor Plan (RS-1), as I mentioned.
“RS-1 is not just planning on paper, but the delivery (project) that we have made, and we feel very proud as it is not just a government project, but an initiative from a private company that also received assistance and support from the state government,” he said.
NSIP, which has received several recognitions, covers approximately 368.26 hectares of prime land with a total gross development value of RM10.2 billion.
As the inaugural development under the IDRISS masterplan, NSIP remains a major contributor to the development of South Selangor as a strategic industrial corridor for high-impact investments and is well positioned to accelerate socio-economic and industrial growth across the region. — Bernama
